name: Trace a basic web request
description: Explain how a URL leads from a browser request to a server response and rendered page without confusing the browser with the server.

name: Create and inspect a local webpage
description: Create named HTML files in a deliberate folder, open them in a browser, and inspect source and rendered output with browser tools.

name: Choose semantic HTML elements
description: Select elements that express the meaning and relationship of content rather than choosing containers only for appearance.

name: Create navigable document structure
description: Organize headings, landmarks, links, lists, images, and metadata so people and user agents can understand the page.

name: Build an accessible native form
description: Use labels, suitable controls, groups, instructions, required states, and error feedback that remain understandable by keyboard and assistive technology users.

name: Represent tabular data semantically
description: Use tables only for related row-and-column data and provide headers and captions that expose relationships.

name: Reason about the CSS cascade
description: Use origin, importance, specificity, source order, and inheritance to explain why a declaration wins.

name: Control boxes and readable type
description: Apply box sizing, dimensions, spacing, borders, color, fonts, line height, and measure without breaking content.

name: Build one-dimensional layouts with Flexbox
description: Use axes, wrapping, alignment, growth, shrinkage, and basis to arrange interface groups.

name: Build two-dimensional layouts with Grid
description: Define tracks, gaps, placement, and responsive grids while choosing Grid or Flexbox according to the relationship.

name: Implement mobile-first responsive layouts
description: Begin from constrained content, add breakpoints when the layout needs them, and preserve priority and operability across viewports.

name: Deliver responsive images and touch-friendly controls
description: Use fluid media, suitable image sources, viewport configuration, and minimum interaction targets without distorting content.

name: Trace JavaScript execution with basic data
description: Predict how values, types, variables, expressions, and operators are evaluated in a short program.

name: Control program flow
description: Use conditionals and loops to express bounded decisions and repetition while avoiding accidental infinite work.

name: Design focused JavaScript functions
description: Define parameters, return values, and responsibilities so behavior can be reused and tested without relying on hidden global state.

name: Organize browser code with modules
description: Export and import named responsibilities while reasoning about local, function, block, and module scope.

name: Model frontend data with arrays and objects
description: Choose arrays for ordered collections and objects for named properties, then access, update, copy, destructure, and compare them deliberately.

name: Transform collections with array methods
description: Use map, filter, find, some, every, and reduce where their output matches the intended data transformation.

name: Manipulate the DOM safely
description: Select elements, create and remove nodes, update text, attributes, and classes, and avoid unsafe HTML insertion for untrusted content.

name: Design event-driven interactions
description: Handle events, default behavior, propagation, delegation, and small UI state transitions without duplicate or inaccessible controls.

name: Implement usable client-side form behavior
description: Read form data, validate rules, present field-specific feedback, preserve input after failure, and distinguish client validation from server authority.

name: Use browser storage deliberately
description: Store, parse, update, and remove non-sensitive local data while recognizing origin scope, string serialization, and privacy limits.

name: Interpret frontend HTTP exchanges
description: Read URLs, methods, status codes, headers, and JSON response shapes at the depth needed to collaborate from an API contract.

name: Coordinate asynchronous fetch flows
description: Use promises and async/await to fetch, parse, validate, cancel or ignore stale work, and surface loading, empty, success, and error states.

name: Diagnose frontend failures systematically
description: Reproduce a defect, reduce its scope, inspect evidence, form a falsifiable hypothesis, and verify the smallest repair.

name: Handle expected JavaScript failures
description: Use thrown errors and targeted try/catch boundaries while preserving useful messages and avoiding silent failure.

name: Architect a small vanilla web application
description: Separate data access, state, rendering, and interaction responsibilities while keeping the application explainable without a framework.

name: Deliver a resilient API-backed feature
description: Implement requirements across responsive, accessible, async, empty, error, persistence, and documentation concerns.

name: Manage source history with Git
description: Inspect working-tree state, stage intentional changes, write meaningful commits, branch, merge, pull, push, and resolve a basic conflict without discarding work.

name: Collaborate through GitHub pull requests
description: Publish a branch, explain its scope, review a diff, respond to feedback, and merge through a pull-request workflow.

name: Operate a Node and npm project
description: Explain Node’s tooling role, read package.json, install dependencies, run scripts, and distinguish project dependencies from generated node_modules content.

name: Use Vite development and build workflows
description: Create, serve, debug, build, preview, and configure a minimal frontend project while understanding bundling, transformation, source maps, and client environment variables conceptually.

name: Model application data with TypeScript
description: Use primitive, object, array, union, optional, literal, and reusable types at the boundary where they clarify JavaScript assumptions.

name: Narrow values and type functions
description: Type parameters and returns, use control-flow narrowing, and distinguish compile-time checking from runtime validation.

name: Type browser APIs safely
description: Handle nullable DOM queries, specific element capabilities, event targets, form data, and reusable generic helpers without unsafe global assertions.

name: Validate external data at runtime
description: Treat parsed JSON as untrusted, check required shapes, and produce typed success/failure results for the rest of the application.

name: Design valuable automated tests
description: Choose test boundaries, arrange inputs, act, assert observable outcomes, and cover normal, boundary, failure, and regression behavior.

name: Test DOM behavior from the user perspective
description: Query by roles and labels, simulate meaningful interactions, await asynchronous outcomes, and avoid coupling tests to private implementation details.

name: Model interfaces as React components
description: Divide a design into purposeful components whose boundaries reflect repeated or independently meaningful UI responsibilities.

name: Render declarative UI with JSX and props
description: Translate semantic HTML into JSX, pass read-only inputs, compose children, and render data without mutating props.

name: Model local React state intentionally
description: Choose the minimal state that changes over time and derive everything else during rendering when possible.

name: Update React state safely from events
description: Use event handlers and state setters with immutable object/array updates and functional updates when the next value depends on the previous one.

name: Build controlled React forms
description: Connect labels, values, change events, constraints, validation feedback, submission states, and recovery without losing native form behavior.

name: Choose and lift shared state
description: Place state at the closest common owner, pass values and handlers explicitly, and avoid contradictory copies across components.

name: Use React Effects for external synchronization
description: Distinguish rendering and events from Effects, declare dependencies, clean up subscriptions or requests, and remove Effects that only derive state.

name: Build resilient React data flows
description: Coordinate route/prop inputs, request lifecycles, stale results, cached intent, and accessible loading, empty, error, and retry states.

name: Implement client-side routing
description: Define route hierarchies, layouts, parameters, navigation, not-found behavior, and direct-load expectations with a maintained React router.

name: Use URLs as appropriate application state
description: Represent shareable navigation, path parameters, and search/filter state in URLs while distinguishing it from local or server state.

name: Extract reusable React logic with custom Hooks
description: Share stateful synchronization or behavior through Hooks while keeping Hook calls valid, inputs explicit, and component output local.

name: Choose local, lifted, and contextual state
description: Distinguish local UI, derived, URL, server, and broadly shared state, then choose the smallest ownership mechanism that fits.

name: Translate design artifacts into implementation decisions
description: Inspect spacing, type, tokens, components, states, responsiveness, and missing specifications, then ask bounded clarification questions.

name: Build accessible React components
description: Preserve native semantics, keyboard operation, focus, names, states, contrast, motion preferences, and restrained ARIA across reusable components.

name: Test React components through behavior
description: Render components with realistic providers, query accessible output, interact as a user, and assert visible outcomes rather than component internals.

name: Test asynchronous and routed React flows
description: Control network boundaries, await state transitions, isolate test state, and verify navigation, errors, retries, and accessibility-relevant behavior.

name: Measure and improve frontend performance
description: Use network, performance, Lighthouse, and Core Web Vitals evidence to prioritize images, loading, rendering, caching, and bundle improvements.

name: Apply frontend security boundaries
description: Avoid unsafe HTML, exposed secrets, token myths, untrusted output, careless dependencies, and authentication/authorization confusion.

name: Automate critical browser journeys
description: Use Playwright locators, isolated test data, web-first assertions, cross-browser projects, and traces for a small high-value end-to-end suite.

name: Deploy and diagnose a frontend application
description: Configure a free-enough static host, SPA route fallback, HTTPS/domain concepts, environment values, build logs, and rollback-aware verification.

name: Plan and communicate frontend work
description: Clarify requirements, identify risks, break scope into tasks, estimate, report progress, document blockers, and negotiate a smaller safe slice when needed.

name: Collaborate across design and backend boundaries
description: Resolve design ambiguity and API contract questions with explicit request, response, error, authentication, state, and responsibility decisions.

name: Frame and architect an independent frontend product
description: Define users, problem, scope, flows, routes, components, data contracts, states, accessibility, testing, performance, and deployment constraints.

name: Build a risk-first vertical slice
description: Implement one thin production path across UI, state, API, validation, tests, and deployment to validate architecture before expanding scope.

name: Implement a production-style React application independently
description: Deliver planned routes, components, forms, state, API behavior, and responsive states with explainable architecture and controlled scope.

name: Operate quality gates during delivery
description: Use typecheck, lint/format policy, unit/integration/E2E tests, accessibility review, performance measurement, security review, and code review as release evidence.

name: Release and operate a frontend product
description: Complete production validation, deployment, smoke monitoring, rollback/redeploy, documentation, and issue triage for a frontend release.

name: Present and defend frontend engineering evidence
description: Explain product scope, architecture, trade-offs, accessibility, testing, performance, debugging, collaboration, and limitations using deployed work and source history.
